records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:56 — The remove action discards the DELETE promise, so failed removals are unhandled and the admin receives no indication that membership was unchanged.
records.rationale: The diff shows `removeMember` action calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` without handling the returned promise. The model's `removeMember` performs a DELETE ajax call whose `.then` only reloads members on success; on failure nothing notifies the user and the member list silently stays stale. The mechanism described (discarded promise, unhandled failure) is directly verifiable in the diff.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:64 — The add action discards the PUT promise, so failed additions are unhandled and the admin receives no indication that membership was unchanged.
records.rationale: The diff shows `addMembers: function() { ... this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames")); }` which discards the returned promise; the model's addMembers performs the PUT and reloads members only on success, so a failed add (e.g. 422 for automatic group or unknown user) results in an unhandled rejection with no error surfaced to the admin, leaving the UI silently unchanged. Mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:31 — Overlapping pagination or membership refresh requests can complete out of order and overwrite newer members and offsets with stale results.
records.rationale: findMembers issues an unkeyed ajax request and unconditionally setProperties(user_count, offset, members) on resolution; rapid next/previous/add/removeMember calls (all call findMembers) can resolve out of order and write stale offset/members over newer results. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff — no request ordering or cancellation guard exists. Whether it materially manifests in practice is harder to confirm, so moderate confidence.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — Editing a group name before adding or removing members commits the membership change by ID but reloads the unsaved name, leaving the displayed members stale after a failed lookup.
records.rationale: The diff shows addMembers/removeMember use the group id ('/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json') while the subsequent findMembers reload fetches by this.get('name'). If the name field is edited but unsaved, the reload hits /groups/<unsaved-name>/members.json which will fail or return the wrong group's members, leaving the displayed member list stale. The mechanism is visible in the diff (group.js findMembers vs addMembers), though the actual failure depends on runtime behavior I cannot fully verify.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — The removeMember success handler does not return the reload promise, so it reports completion before refresh and cannot propagate a refresh failure, leaving stale members displayed.
records.rationale: The diff shows removeMember's success handler calls self.findMembers() without returning it ('}).then(function() { // reload member list self.findMembers(); });'), so the promise returned to callers resolves before the refresh completes and any refresh rejection is swallowed. This is factually accurate and specific to new code in the diff. It is not a demonstrable defect (the admin controller's removeMember action ignores the return value, so no incorrect behavior is observable there), but it is a legitimate, concrete promise-chaining concern for newly added nontrivial logic.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:58 — The addMembers success handler does not return the reload promise, so it reports completion before refresh and cannot propagate a refresh failure, leaving stale members displayed.
records.rationale: The diff shows `addMembers` ends with `.then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` — the reload promise is not returned, so the promise from addMembers resolves before the member list actually refreshes, and a refresh failure is swallowed. Same pattern exists in removeMember but the finding specifically cites addMembers line 58, which matches. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff, though no caller in this diff currently awaits the result, so impact is modest.
